note: The setup step table is the single source of ordering and source/investigator applicability. PDF preparation uses the host visual reader; no OCR or text bundle is required. System instructions are English; the setup assistant speaks the player language.

templates.unknown_step: There is no step named {step}. Available steps: {available}. Next: {next}
templates.needs_unmet: {step} is not available yet: finish {missing} first. Next: {next}
templates.already_done: {step} is already done (receipt {receipt}); it is not repeated. Next: {next}
templates.all_done: Setup is complete and the campaign is ready. Open the table: {launch}

starter.description: one of campaign.list's starter names (kernel.hello content.modules)

module.description: an id from module.list with status: installed -- an already-built book; preparation reuses its material and settles this campaign's opening

pdf.description: the original local PDF path; the host will read its pages visually

lines.do: Ask the player to pick a starter (the list from kernel.hello), an already-installed module (module.list, status: installed), or to give an original PDF path.
lines.next: Choose the source: name a starter, name an installed module, or give an original PDF path.

module_id.description: a previously registered module, if available

start_scene.description: an authored opening chosen after candidates were returned

lines.do: Prepare source guidance or reuse accepted guidance. In frontend setup the host completes this step as soon as reviewed guidance is accepted, while the opening prepares in the background. For multiple authored openings, match the player intent to the candidate summaries and select one before creating the campaign.
lines.next: Prepare the chosen PDF with prepare-module; if reading is still in progress, wait for the existing job rather than starting another.

module.description: starter id, or the module id source preparation returned (carried automatically)

play_language.description: BCP-47 tag of the language the keeper plays in: zh-Hans | en (default zh-Hans); the kernel writes nothing in it

lines.do: campaign.create: status setting_up; a starter is registered into the module store at the same time.
lines.next: Create the campaign: give a campaign id (and an optional title).

profile.description: Semantic object: name, occupation (catalog id), age, sex, concept, occupation_skills (8 distinct concrete catalog names), interest_skills (selected concrete names), own_language (actual language), era (optional rulebook period from returned options; the agent chooses it from source context), backstory (3-6 of personal_description/ideology_beliefs/significant_people/meaningful_locations/treasured_possessions/traits plus scenario_bound), key_connection {backstory_field,summary}, equipment [ordinary item names], weapons [optional rulebook profile names], aptitude {strong:[ABBR],weak:[ABBR]} when the player's own words call this person notably strong or notably poor in body or mind (characteristic abbreviations only; the kernel assigns this player's own rolled results accordingly and promises no value). On edits send only changed fields. No numeric skills/cash.

defaults.source_note: Legacy setup.investigator defaults only. Conversational setup.draft uses standard rolled characteristics and formula-based skill budgets.

allocation.source_note: Occupation-point policy (#21), content not code. spread: walk the occupation's skill list in the book's order, raising every entry to tiers[0], then tiers[1], then the starting cap (skills.json guided_creation_policy.starting_skill_cap); an entry the kernel cannot name (a rulebook choice such as 'any one other skill' or a group such as 'Firearms') is reserved the tier's value as unspent for the table's development family instead of the points piling onto the four skills it can name. fill: the earlier one-point round-robin over the resolvable entries only, kept as an option. The tiers are a table-feel choice (a rounded investigator over four maxed skills), not rulebook numbers.

interest_allocation.source_note: Personal-interest policy, content not code, and the same walk #21 gave the occupational list. spread: walk the supplied interest_skills in order, raising every entry to tiers[0], then tiers[1], then the starting cap; fill: the older one-point round-robin, kept as an option. Only a model-supplied interest_skills list is ordered by what the player said matters, so only that list takes the tiered walk; the legacy auto-pool is the era's standard sheet in table order and keeps the round-robin.

aptitude.source_note: Who the emphasis came from, content not code. player: the player's own words named this characteristic. concept: the setup model read it off the person the player described, which is legitimate but is an inference, so the card records it as one and the model never reports it as something the player said. Both origins place the same rolls identically; concept_limit caps an inferred emphasis at that many strong and that many weak so reading a person does not optimize every card into its occupation's archetype and retire the dice. A longer emphasis has to come from the player.

formulas.source_note: Keeper Rulebook Chapter 3, personal interest skill points = INT x 2 (investigator-create-contract.json skill_budget description).

interest_pool.source_note: Keeper Rulebook Chapter 3: no points may be put into Cthulhu Mythos at creation; Credit Rating is set from the occupation's range.

lines.do: Compute a complete draft from the player concept with setup.draft after the follow-up answer (one follow-up by default, spent on an aptitude direction that steers the skill choices; a second only for a genuine gap; immediately when the player delegated the remaining choices). Propose rather than ask whatever you can: the way into the opening, personal ties, age, ordinary gear. Complete ordinary missing semantic choices yourself at draft time. The tool returns actual values for the host to show. Do not ask the player for numbers. Do not claim a card is committed yet.
lines.next: Prepare or revise the full investigator draft using profile. On missing catalog names fix them using returned options in the same turn.

consent.description: approved after the player confirms the displayed card; delegated only for an explicit write-now or modify-and-write request

pending_action.description: Only when the player requested an adventure action before setup finished: quote the actual requested action verbatim, to preserve it for the Keeper. Do not invent an action or treat identity as commission acceptance.

lines.do: Confirm the current draft only with explicit player approval or write-now delegation. The host injects its revision. Then complete setup.
lines.next: Wait for approval or modify the draft. Do not confirm on an ordinary character description.

lines.do: investigator.list returns every card in the investigator library (name, occupation, era, HP/SAN, last campaign and turn, newest first); read it out and let the player choose one by its library_id, or say they would rather build a new investigator instead (create-investigator).
lines.next: List the library (investigator.list) so the player can choose a card, or use create-investigator for a brand-new one.

campaign.description: filled in automatically from the campaign already being set up

library_id.description: one of the library_id values investigator.list returned

as.description: optional: play this card under a new name, which mints it a row of its own (a second person, not a rename) instead of sharing the original's

lines.do: investigator.load copies the chosen card's sheet into this campaign byte for byte -- no conversion, no re-roll, no era gate (contract §21.3); occupation and point allocation are skipped because the sheet already carries them.
lines.next: Load the investigator: give the library_id to use (from browse-library's list).

lines.do: setup.complete: require the confirmed card and the selected opening. If opening_preparing is returned, end the reply and retain confirmation; the frontend will retry when ready. Otherwise write the handoff receipt and enter ready_for_table.
